headline: High: Dexter’s broad egress plus PaddleOCR’s browser/API processing creates default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can autonomously execute and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while PaddleOCR runs browsers and processes documents/images. If Dexter feeds untrusted web or document content into PaddleOCR, instruction-like text can be reinterpreted. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Dexter passes untrusted document or web text into PaddleOCR without provenance filtering, prompt injection is plausible.
IF both agents share a workspace or clipboard bridge, the attack surface increases.
mitigations: Restrict PaddleOCR inputs to trusted files only.
Add a provenance tag to every Dexter-generated artifact.
Disable browser automation for untrusted sources.
Review scratchpad contents before handing them to PaddleOCR.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; PaddleOCR processes documents/images and has allowlisted egress. If sensitive files or extracted text flow from Dexter into PaddleOCR, either agent can expose data through outbound APIs. The pair lacks documented isolation, so default handling is risky.
conditions: IF Dexter sends financial or market data into PaddleOCR, sensitive content can leave the local boundary.
IF PaddleOCR uploads extracted document text to external APIs, leakage extends beyond the original workspace.
mitigations: Limit both agents to a segregated test dataset.
Remove secrets from the runtime environment before processing.
Block outbound network except to approved endpoints.
Redact sensitive fields before OCR or analysis.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace or shared outputs, they can overwrite or race on artifacts. No locking or coordination is documented, so conflict is plausible but not clearly high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or file set, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
IF Dexter launches multiple instances against PaddleOCR outputs, overwrite conflicts become more likely.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a simple file lock.
Use unique filenames per run.
Disable concurrent Dexter instances on shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous execution can generate outputs that PaddleOCR may consume as document-processing input. If PaddleOCR treats those outputs as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream OCR/translation results. The pairwise pathway is inferred from docs-only profiles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR consumes Dexter output without verification, upstream mistakes propagate downstream.
IF Dexter emits malformed or fabricated document content, PaddleOCR may preserve the error in extracted text.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Compare OCR output against source documents.
Reject low-confidence Dexter outputs before OCR.
Log provenance for every handoff.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between generation and parsing.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and handles multiple API keys, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If regulated financial or personal documents are routed through PaddleOCR’s external APIs or Dexter’s broad egress, retention and residency obligations may diverge. No compliance controls are documented for either agent, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF regulated documents or financial records are processed through external APIs, residency/retention obligations may be violated.
IF either agent logs inputs longer than policy allows, deletion/export obligations can fail.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of external APIs.
Set short log-retention windows.
Document a deletion workflow for both tools.
requires-engineering: align both agents to the same compliance policy and DPA terms.
